answer.rationale: Before committing, I want the original record for c2 (the low-cost vendor onboarding experience) and c1 (the incumbent stability precedent) because both directly bear on the central trade-off: switching to the low-cost vendor meets the 18% mandate per the quote, but the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer — exactly the kind of moment where c1-style stability logic argues for caution and c2-style onboarding speed argues for action. Verifying both originals is necessary, not nice-to-have, because they are the only inherited observations that speak to a vendor switch under tight operating conditions. After verification I will decide whether to fully switch primary supply to the low-cost vendor, or — if the original records show onboarding friction I cannot absorb at 94% utilization — to negotiate terms against the low-cost quote using the c4 benchmarking precedent. I am not yet committing to action; I am reserving the right to pivot to negotiate_terms based on what the archives return. I am also explicitly not yet committed to a scale larger than a small guarded test, because the 94% utilization with no buffer means a full-scale switch on day 71 would concentrate delivery risk in a way the inherited memory does not authorize me to ignore.
